newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen steady, focus on retail.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen steady, focus on retail.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen steady on Thursday, with the market likely to focus on retailers Matahari and Multipolar following the purchase of a stake in Multipolar by a retail tycoon, brokers said.
"Wall Street's rise overnight coupled with the purchase reports are likely to further boost market sentiment after a modest rise in the index yesterday," one broker said.
PT Multipolar Corporation said Matahari president-director Hari Dharmawan has bought a 10-percent stake in Multipolar in his personal capacity.

"Hari Dharmawan in his personal capacity through his personal holding company PT Haritama Bakti Persada has purchased 10 percent of Multipolar shares for 56 billion rupiah or 2,025 rupiah per share from the Lippo Group," Multipolar said in a statement received on Thursday.
Brokers said the 2,025 rupiah per share purchase was likely to boost sentiment in Multipolar as Multipolar's closing price on the regular board was 1,450 rupiah on Wednesday.
Other stocks to watch included Bank Servitia on a sharp rise in its 1996 net profit, they said.
Bank BNI was also likely to remain active following a rebound on Wednesday and an estimated increase in its first quarter earnings, they said.
On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index rose 1.55 points, or 0.24 percent, to close at 632.82 points.
Heavyweight cigarette manufacturers Sampoerna and Gudang Garam made modest gains following the bargain-hunting, brokers said.
The most actively traded Multipolar MLPL, the retail unit of the Lippo Group conglomerate, rose 50 rupiah to 1,500 rupiah, with volume approaching six million shares.
Dharmawan, president and founder of Matahari, bought a 10-percent stake in Multipolar for 56 billion rupiah, or 2,025 rupiah per share, in his personal capacity, Multipolar said.
Multipolar has a controlling stake in Matahari.
